Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nosъ, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂s.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nos]
  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

нос • (nos) m inan (genitive но́са, nominative plural насы́, genitive plural насо́ў)

  1. nose

Bulgarian

[edit]
Bulgarian Wikipedia has an article on:
нос
Wikipedia bg

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nosъ, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂s.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nɔs]
  • Audio (Standard Bulgarian):(file)
  • Rhymes: -ɔs

Noun

[edit]

нос • (nos) m

  1. nose
  2. (of a shoe) toe
  3. (of a ship) bow, head, prow
  4. (geography) cape, promontory, foreland, gore

  • (diminutive) носе́ (nosé)

  • (diminutive) носе́ц (noséc)
  • (augmentative) но́сище (nósište)

  • носо- (noso-) (in compounds)

  • но́сест (nósest)

    • дългоно́с (dǎlgonós, “with long nose”)
    • кривоно́с (krivonós, “with crooked nose”)
    • кукуно́с (kukunós, “with hook nose”)
    • остроно́с (ostronós, “with pointy nose”)
    • чипоно́с (čiponós, “with maimed nose”)

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nosъ, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂s.

Pronunciation

[edit]

  • Audio:(file)

Noun

[edit]

нос • (nos) m (plural носови, relational adjective носен or назален, diminutive носе)

  1. nose
  2. (geography) cape, promontory, headland

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Old Slovak nos, from Proto-Slavic *nosъ, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂s. Cognates include Carpathian Rusyn нус (nus) and Slovak nos.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [ˈnɔs]
  • Rhymes: -ɔs
  • Hyphenation: нос

Noun

[edit]

нос (nos) m inan (diminutive нощок or носик, relational adjective носни or носови)

  1. nose
    видуц нос ― viduc nos ― to blow the nose
    нє хпай нос до моїх стварох
    nje xpaj nos do mojix stvarox
    don't poke your nose into my stuff
  2. (nautical) bow, rostrum (front of a boat or ship)
  3. snout, muzzle
    Synonyms: нозґер (nozger), писки (piski), рило (rilo)

Declension

[edit]
Declension of нос (nos)
singular plural
nominative нос (nos) носи (nosi)
genitive носа (nosa) носох (nosox)
dative носу (nosu) носом (nosom)
accusative нос (nos) носи (nosi)
instrumental носом (nosom) носами (nosami)
locative носу (nosu) носох (nosox)
vocative носу (nosu) носи (nosi)

Related terms

[edit]
adjectives
  • носати (nosati)
nouns
  • носороґ m anim (nosorog)

  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “nose”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 190
  • Fejsa, M.; Šlemender, M.; Čelʹovski, S. (2022), “snout”, in Анґлийско-руски словнїк [English-Rusyn Dictionary] (in Pannonian Rusyn), Novi Sad: Faculty of Philosophy; Ruska matka, →ISBN, page 288

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • носъ (nos) — pre-1918 spelling

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Slavic *nosъ, from Proto-Indo-European *néh₂s. Cognate with English nose.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): [nos]
  • Audio:(file)
  • Audio (Saint Petersburg):(file)
  • Rhymes: -os

Noun

[edit]

нос • (nos) m inan (genitive но́са, nominative plural носы́, genitive plural носо́в, relational adjective носово́й, diminutive но́сик or носо́к, augmentative носи́ще or нося́ра or носи́на, expressive term нося́мба)

  1. nose
    У него́ кровь идёт из но́са ― U nevó krovʹ idjót iz nósa ― His nose is bleeding.
  2. bow, prow (boats)
  3. forepart, point
  4. horn (of an anvil)
  5. headland, promontory, point (geology)
  6. lip (for pouring)

Declension

  • под нос (pod nos)

Compound words:

  • долгоно́сик m anim (dolgonósik)

  • носопы́рка f (nosopýrka)
  • носоро́г m anim (nosoróg)
  • ухогорлоно́с m anim (uxogorlonós)

Compounds:

  • води́ть за́ нос impf (vodítʹ zá nos)
  • вороти́ть нос impf (vorotítʹ nos)
  • да́льше своего́ но́са (dálʹše svojevó nósa)
  • да́льше со́бственного но́са (dálʹše sóbstvennovo nósa)
  • держа́ть нос по́ ветру impf (deržátʹ nos pó vetru)
  • задра́ть нос pf (zadrátʹ nos), задира́ть нос impf (zadirátʹ nos)
  • заруби́ть на носу́ pf (zarubítʹ na nosú), заруби́ть себе́ на носу́ pf (zarubítʹ sebé na nosú)
  • нос к но́су (nos k nósu)
  • но́сом зе́млю рыть impf (nósom zémlju rytʹ)
  • пове́сить нос pf (povésitʹ nos)
  • получи́ть по́ носу pf (polučítʹ pó nosu)
  • сова́ть нос impf (sovátʹ nos)
  • утере́ть нос pf (uterétʹ nos)
  • щёлкнуть по́ носу pf (ščólknutʹ pó nosu)
Phrases

  • нос не доро́с (nos ne dorós)
Proverbs

Related via Proto-Indo-European *néh₂s:
